I want to know if toxic lagoon fire caused my husband's rare deadly cancer
stories.summary: Steve Williams died of lung cancer 14 years after falling in to a lagoon at a toxic waste dump fire. It was a sight which struck terror into the firefighters called to tackle it - a blazing chemical waste lagoon on fire, with barrels exploding into the air. Steve Williams, then in his 20s, was one of 60 firefighters sent to tackle the burning Llwyneinion lagoon in August 1980, which was sending thick black smoke over a nearby village. Steve slipped in and, although he was pulled out, his widow thinks what he swallowed may have cost him his life from a rare form of lung cancer aged 39. She said "someone should be held accountable".

stories.summary: The farm's alpacas and Valais Blacknose sheep make the pupils at the local school relaxed and happy. An autistic boy who also has ADHD has helped turn his alpaca farm into a safe haven for other children with special educational needs. Hayden Geraghty, 16, and his mother Caroline welcome children and adults to their farm in Limavady, County Londonderry, for what is known as alpaca therapy. The farm at the foot of Binevenagh mountain also has Valais Blacknose sheep and the animals are taken to visit Hayden's school. Health experts and charities have said working with alpacas can be therapeutic, reduce anxiety and improve someone's mental and emotional well-being.
